memos.headline: Momentum Leaders S07, S05, S08 Near Highs but Stretched; S01 and S02 in Structural Downtrends
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe as of 10/31. The strongest momentum names—S07 (+88% over 26w, RSI 73.5), S05 (+75% over 26w, RSI 77.2), and S10 (+86% over 26w, RSI 66.5)—are all trading well above their 200-day means (48%, 46%, 37% respectively) and near 52-week highs, but the degree of extension raises mean-reversion risk, particularly for S05 and S07 where RSI is above 73. I have the most conviction in S08, which combines strong trend (+22.9% over 12w, +15% relative strength vs SPY) with a more moderate RSI of 69 and only 9% above its 50-day mean, making it the cleanest risk/reward among the leaders. On the weak side, S01 is -16.3% from its 52-week high, below both moving averages, with negative relative strength on every timeframe—a textbook avoid until it reclaims its 200-day mean. S02 is the most damaged name in the universe at -45.4% from its high and trading 11.6% below its 200-day mean; the 12-week +39.6% bounce looks like a bear-market rally within a broken structure, and I would need to see price sustain above the 200-day average before reconsidering.

views.note: Strong uptrend near 52w high with RSI 69 and +15% 12w relative strength vs SPY; would reassess on a close below the 50-day mean (~248).
Sitting at a fresh 52w high (0% drawdown), RSI 67, and +9.3% 4w relative strength; trend is clean and I'd stay long above ~225 (50-day area).
Massive momentum (+43% in 12w) and dominant relative strength, but RSI 77.2 and 15% above 50d mean signal overextension; waiting for a pullback toward the 50d mean (~244) to get involved.

Flat 12w return (-0.6%), negative relative strength vs SPY on 4w and 12w, RSI 47.7—no directional edge; needs to break above 52w high (~542) or break below 200d mean (~461) to generate a signal.
Mild uptrend but losing relative strength vs SPY (-1.6% 4w); RSI 59 is mid-range—no compelling setup either way.

Below both moving averages (-2.3% vs 50d, -6.5% vs 200d), -16.3% from 52w high, persistent negative relative strength; would reconsider only on a sustained close above the 200d mean (~161).
Catastrophic -45.4% drawdown from 52w high, below 200d mean by 11.6%, RSI 40.3 and falling; the 12w bounce looks like a bear rally and I'd need price above ~385 (200d area) to reconsider.

memos.headline: S10 and S05 Show Superior Earnings Power; S02 and S09 Flash Cash-Flow Compression Warnings
memos.body: I see a stark divergence in earnings quality across the universe this quarter. S10 stands out with 56.5% net margins, +55.6% YoY revenue growth, and minimal debt of $8.47B—this is the cleanest earnings profile in the group. S05 is similarly impressive at 34.2% net margin on $102.35B revenue with net income up 33.0% YoY and only $14.79B in total debt. On the other end, S02 posted a 2.1% net margin with net income collapsing 61.2% YoY despite 12.2% revenue growth, signaling severe margin compression against $80.14B of debt—I cannot pay for that. S09 is also deteriorating with revenue down 12.4% and net income down 23.4% on an 8.7% margin, while S06 carries $419.80B in total debt alongside declining revenue and earnings, which demands caution.

views.note: 56.5% net margin, +55.6% revenue growth, near-zero leverage at $8.47B debt—best earnings power in the universe; would reassess if margins compress below 45%.
34.2% net margin with +33.0% YoY net income growth and low debt of $14.79B on $102B revenue is durable and high-quality.
35.7% net margin, +18.4% revenue growth, and manageable $43.21B debt make this a solid compounder; would watch for margin fade below 30%.
Revenue of $167.70B growing 13.3% is impressive but 10.8% net margin is thin for the scale; need to see margin expansion to get constructive.
24.9% net margin and 9.6% revenue growth are solid but $91.80B in total debt and decelerating growth keep me on the sideline.
21.2% net margin and +20% net income growth are encouraging, but only 3% revenue growth and $24.32B debt on $22B revenue limit upside conviction.
Net margin collapsed to 2.1% with net income down 61.2% YoY despite revenue growing 12.2%—severe cost or impairment issues against $80.14B debt.
Revenue declining 12.4% with net income down 23.4% and an 8.7% margin signals cyclical or structural headwinds I don't want to own.
$419.80B in total debt dwarfs the $44.91B revenue base, and both revenue (-10.5%) and net income (-17.4%) are shrinking—leverage risk is too high.
Flat revenue (-0.7%) and net income down 18.7% with $31.74B debt on $16.57B revenue suggest margin erosion with no near-term catalyst.

memos.headline: Fed Easing Cycle Intact but Sticky 3% CPI and Rising Unemployment Signal a Cautious Slowdown Regime
memos.body: I see the macro regime as mid-cycle easing into a softening labor market: the fed funds upper bound is now 4.00%, down 100bp over 12 months, while the unemployment rate has risen 30bp over both 3- and 12-month horizons to 4.40%. CPI is running at 3.0% y/y, which remains above target and limits the pace of further cuts—this is not a clean easing backdrop. The 10y yield at 4.11% has declined 26bp over three months and the 10y-2y spread has steepened to +50bp, consistent with the market pricing a gradual normalization rather than recession. I favor duration-sensitive growth and defensive staples over banks (whose NIM tailwind fades as the curve steepens modestly) and pure cyclicals (where rising unemployment is a headwind). A CPI print dropping below 2.5% y/y or unemployment breaching 4.7% would shift my call toward a more aggressive easing/recession regime.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth benefits from falling front-end rates and declining 10y yields; easing cycle supports valuations.
Defensive staples outperform in a slowdown regime with rising unemployment and still-elevated inflation limiting aggressive risk-taking.
Banks see modest NIM pressure as the curve steepens only 6bp over 3 months and further rate cuts compress the short end.
Cyclicals face headwinds from a 30bp rise in unemployment over three months signaling demand softening.
Rate-sensitive sectors benefit as the easing cycle continues; lower 10y yields support asset-heavy business models.
Energy lacks a clear macro tailwind—slowing growth dampens demand expectations while inflation remains above target.

memos.headline: Earnings-Season Price Reactions Split Sharply: S03 and S07 Surge While S04 and S06 Sink
memos.body: I am reading the post-earnings price reactions across the universe as the clearest sentiment signal available this cycle. S03 (+9.6%) and S07 (+11.6%) posted outsized positive moves on their results filings, suggesting a genuine narrative shift to the upside that likely has not fully been arbitraged yet given the recency of the prints. S04 (-2.9%) and S06 (-1.9%) moved negatively on their results, and with no offsetting positive catalysts in the filing stream, the tone around those names looks like it is deteriorating. S08's essentially flat reaction (-0.4%) and S01's muted +0.2% tell me the market had already priced in whatever those reports contained, leaving little directional edge. I have highest conviction on S03 and S07 where the magnitude of the moves signals a clear sentiment inflection, and I would avoid S04 where the negative reaction coincides with a recent management change filing.

views.note: A +9.6% one-day reaction to the 10/30 earnings 8-K signals a strong positive sentiment inflection that may still have room to run.
The +11.6% move on the 10/29 results filing is the largest in the universe and points to a decisive upward narrative shift.
A -2.9% reaction to earnings plus a recent director departure filing suggest deteriorating sentiment around this name.
The -1.9% earnings reaction on 10/14 and no positive follow-through in subsequent filings leave tone negative; bylaws amendment adds governance noise.
A +2.5% post-earnings move is modestly positive but not as decisive as S03/S07; lean constructive with lower conviction.
The -0.4% reaction to the 10/30 earnings print is essentially noise; sentiment appears fully priced.
A +0.2% move on Q1 results and multiple Reg FD filings suggest the market already digested the news; no edge here.
The +0.5% earnings-day reaction is tepid and the earlier Reg FD filings add no incremental directional signal.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Easing but Oil Weakness Signals Demand-Side Geopolitical Risk
memos.body: I note that the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index has dropped 31% over the past month to 280, suggesting a near-term de-escalation in trade/sanctions rhetoric, though the level remains elevated at +2.1% over three months. WTI crude at $61.36 is down nearly 14% over three months, which I read as a demand-side signal consistent with slowing global activity—possibly reflecting the cumulative drag of export controls and supply-chain reshoring rather than a supply glut. VIX at 16.91 is creeping higher (+9.2% over 3m) and HY OAS widened modestly, indicating credit markets are not fully complacent. Without specific details in the 8-K filings beyond Reg FD and Other Events disclosures, I have limited company-level geopolitical intelligence, so my conviction is moderate across the board. A renewed escalation in US-China export controls or fresh energy sanctions would change my view materially.

views.note: Two Reg FD filings in October suggest active investor communication but no clear geopolitical catalyst from available evidence.
Late-October Reg FD disclosure coincides with falling policy uncertainty; absent detail on content, I stay neutral.
Two filings in October (Reg FD and Other Events) warrant monitoring but provide no actionable geopolitical signal from available data.
Single Reg FD filing on Oct 29 with no detail; macro backdrop of easing policy uncertainty is mildly supportive but not enough for conviction.
Early-October Reg FD filing with no geopolitical specifics; WTI weakness could be a headwind if energy-exposed.
September filings are stale and the 8-K/A amendment suggests a correction rather than a new event; low conviction either way.
